findings.summary: Corrections to the Hellas record: (1) the presiding NY bankruptcy judge was Hon. Proc. 14-01848 or NY Index 653357/2011, and most likely received a CPEC distribution as a TPG operating partner only. findings.detail: Adv. Proc. 14-01848 (Glenn J), parent Ch.15 Case 12-10631, Hosking I-IV opinions: Hosking I = 524 B.R. 488 (Jan 29 2015) dismissed Apax Europe + Halusa for personal jx + dismissed NYDCL fraudulent transfer for lack of standing under §1521(a)(7); Hosking II = 526 B.R. 499 (Mar 9 2015) §546(e) safe harbor doesn't preempt unjust enrichment; Hosking III = 535 B.R. 543 (Aug 19 2015) permitted FAC adding UK Insolvency Act §§213+423 claims; Hosking IV (Mar 31 2016) denied TPG renewed personal-jx MTD; FNC stay granted Aug 19 2016; adversary terminated Aug 4 2022; Ch.15 closed Nov 21 2022. TPG decision-makers as of December 2006 (FAC ¶24): David Bonderman, James Coulter, and William S. Price III (founders) made all final TPG investment decisions including TIM Hellas; Jonathan Coslet (CIO, named TPG Defendant); Stephen Peel does not appear and is not a named defendant, correcting an earlier framing. TPG affiliate defendants named individually: Schifter, Boyce, Burns, Chang, Coslet, Davis, Dechet, Gates, Haines, Marren, MacDougall, Reinhart, Sisitsky, Taylor, Wheeler, Williams, Viola. Most likely Cushman/Lucid overlap candidates: Todd Sisitsky (TPG healthcare PE) and Jonathan Coslet (TPG CIO). On the TPG Europe execution side: Matthias Calice (signed both redemption agreements + Hellas board); Philippe Costeletos (TPG Europe co-head, Hellas board); Tanguy Serra (supplied 'invented enterprise value' to KPMG); Vincenzo Morelli (warned Coulter Dec 16 2006 of 'precarious position'). Apax decision-makers as of December 2006: Martin Halusa (Apax CEO, dismissed personal jx); John F. Megrue Jr. (Chairman Apax NY, attended Dec 4 2006 IEC meeting); Mitch Truwit (co-CEO Apax). Not named: Adrian Beecroft, Ian Jones, Stephen Grabiner. On the Apax execution side: Giancarlo Aliberti (Apax London, signed both redemption agreements + Hellas board); Frank Ehmer (Oct 17 2006 to DB: 'Come on – we love you guys. Even more so if you up your proposal to €3bn'); Shashank Singh (Dec 2 2006 'putting the business under huge pressure to take their money out a few months early'). Hellas board of managers as of Dec 18 2006: Maurizio Bottinelli, Aliberti, Calice, Costeletos, Guy Harles (Lux lawyer), Benoit Duvieusart (Lux lawyer). On Deutsche Bank's execution side: David Bugge (Dec 3 2006 internal 'concern' email — '[c]oncern... that an aggressive recap overburdens the company and risks the equity at a 2 year exit'); DB earned ~€4.17M underwriting fees. Sale-process bankers: Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers (failed mid-2006 third-party sale, contacted 30+ parties). On valuation: KPMG LLP 'reverse engineered' the Optional Redemption Price based on Tanguy Serra's invented enterprise value (FAC ¶178). Lazard does not appear in the record. Cortlandt St Recovery v Bonderman (NY Index 653357/2011, Reed JSC): March 7 2024 1st Department reversed motion court — held that lumping TPG defendants together under 'collective alter ego' theory was error; each defendant must individually satisfy alter-ego standard. Bloomberg Law: 'TPG Wins $1B Court Case Nears End of Greek Telecom Saga'. Cortlandt's NY-state veil-piercing path against TPG died March 7 2024. Reed JSC March 25 2021 sealing-motion order DENIED both sides' seal motions — Exhibit 11 (alter-ego expert report) and Exhibit 84 (Lux law) should be on unsealed NYSCEF post-March 2021 (viewable only via E-filing logged-in access, not guest preview). SPQR Capital was a noteholder ('bondholders like SPQR with 100 percent losses' per privatefundscfo.com) not just public commenter — confirmed; SPQR not named plaintiff but beneficial holder represented through Wilmington Trust + Cortlandt litigation-funding vehicle. Andrew L. Farkas does NOT appear in Hellas record — separate network from the Cushman EFTA02341745/EFTA02505022 thread, sharing only TPG/Apax as overlapping principals. On Arora's status: he is not a named defendant, and July 2015 Indian-press coverage derives from the FAC's Transferee Class of CPEC holders >$100K. Likely received CPEC distribution as TPG operating partner with personal stake in Hellas vehicle; 'settlement of more than €1m' if exists is private resolution of Transferee Class claim never reduced to filed pleading. Per Plaintiffs' Opposition at 13: 16 videotaped depositions included 'four in the United States, eleven in the U.K., and one in India.' The single India-based deponent fits Arora's profile (a strong inference, not confirmed). The Luxembourg Tribunal d'Arrondissement on 23 Dec 2015 held that CPECs are debt instruments not subject to Lux companies-law illegal-dividend rules (Articles 72/100 of Lux Companies Act 1915); it found no fraud and no illegal dividend, and the English liquidators failed to establish a €973M claim under Lux law. The action was dismissed in TPG/Apax's favor. That Luxembourg ruling was a decisive precedent for the parallel UK and US actions because it established CPEC as debt, foreclosing the 'fraudulent dividend' theory. Counsel of record: Cortlandt = Andrew R. Goldenberg (Levy Goldenberg/Stamell & Schager); Wilmington Trust = Foley & Lardner LLP (Peter N. Wang, Robert A. Scher, Alissa M. Nann, David B. Goroff); TPG = Kasowitz Benson Torres LLP (Marc E. Kasowitz lead since 02/02/2012; Andrew K. Glenn) + Loeb & Loeb (Paul M. O'Connor III); Apax = Ropes & Gray LLP (Robert S. Fischler lead; Stephen C. Moeller-Sally); DB = Cahill Gordon & Reindel; TCW = Latham & Watkins LA (Wayne S. Flick, Amy C. Quartarolo). The Hellas liquidators' plaintiff counsel was Chadbourne & Parke LLP (Howard Seife, Andrew Rosenblatt, Marc D. Ashley, Robert M. Kirby), who described the transaction as a 'duplicitous and catastrophic plunder.' Deal chronology: April 12 2006 Hellas issues €500M PIK Notes due 2014 + 1-for-100 CPEC split + €376.6M to Sponsors; April-Nov 2006 sale process via MS+Lehman fails; Oct 17 2006 DB pitches aggressive recap; Dec 4 2006 Apax IEC meeting; Dec 18 2006 Hellas board CPEC redemption resolutions; Dec 21 2006 Sub Notes issued + Hellas → Sponsors €973,657,610; Feb 2007 sale to Weather Investments S.p.A. (Sawiris) for €500M equity (€6.4M for residual CPECs at €1 par).

section_suggestions.title: Key Relationships
section_suggestions.guidance: Narrative about the most significant relationships. Name each person with a link to their dossier. Explain the nature and significance of each relationship, not just that it exists.

curation.lead:
SPQR Capital Holding SA is a Luxembourg-domiciled investment holding company registered at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register under number B150334, founded by the French finance executive Bertrand Gauquelin des Pallières and chaired from 1 March 2016 by the Italian financier Alessandro Benedetti [Finding #11215][Finding #11221][REG:LU:B150334]. According to NorthData and Luxembourg RCS filings, the company maintained its registered office at 12 rue Guillaume Schneider, L-2522 Luxembourg, the NeoTrust Fiduciary domicile shared with Compagnie Du Saleve SA and at least eleven entities recorded in the ICIJ Panama Papers leak [Finding #11215][Finding #11129][REG:LU:B150334]. The vehicle entered liquidation on 16 March 2023 under court-appointed liquidator Christian Steinmetz [Finding #11215][Finding #11114].

SPQR was formed by a three-person breakaway from Deutsche Bank Principal Finance in 2007 — des Pallières, Malik Chaabouni, and Moez Ben-Zid — and operated as a junior bondholder in the Wind Hellas / TIM Hellas creditor litigation against Naguib Sawiris's Weather Investments, in which SPQR and other subordinated noteholders were reported to have suffered total losses on their position [Finding #11114][Finding #11149][Finding #11221]. According to the Luxembourg RCS director timeline, des Pallières, Benedetti, and the Luxembourg corporate-administration director Mathieu Villaume were appointed to the SPQR board on the same day, 1 March 2016, during the active phase of that creditor activity [Finding #11215][Finding #11226][REG:LU:B150334].

SPQR's Swiss arm, SPQR Capital Services Sagl, was registered in Lugano on 17 March 2011 under company number CHE-496.390.425 with chair Alessandro Benedetti [Finding #11215][Finding #11103]. Until its liquidation, the company served as the central Luxembourg vehicle for the Benedetti–des Pallières group of companies, and the same three-handed director composition recurs across Attali Investment Partners Ltd, Equus Total Return Inc, Cadogan Petroleum plc, and Bitfury Group Limited [Finding #11101][Finding #11103][Finding #11221].
curation.system_role: The company served as a recurring Luxembourg holding vehicle for the Benedetti–des Pallières–Misra group of directors. A single registered office at 12 rue Guillaume Schneider hosted both SPQR and a Rothschild & Co Five Arrows portfolio company, and the same three directors signed for SPQR during the Wind Hellas creditor litigation that overlapped with the SoftBank-era reputational campaigns reported by the Wall Street Journal.

sections.title: Corporate Structure and Registration
sections.content:
SPQR Capital Holding SA was incorporated in Luxembourg under Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register number B150334 and maintained its registered office at 12 rue Guillaume Schneider, L-2522 Luxembourg, the domicile maintained by the corporate-services provider NeoTrust Fiduciary [Finding #11215][REG:LU:B150334]. Luxembourg RCS filings retrieved via NorthData record that the same address simultaneously hosted Compagnie Du Saleve SA (Luxembourg RCS B223232), wholly owned since 8 March 2023 by Five Arrows AutoBench Holding Sàrl, the private-equity arm of Rothschild & Co [Finding #11211][Finding #11129][REG:LU:B223232]. The same address also corresponds to eleven entities indexed in the ICIJ Panama Papers leak, including Kaupthing Bank Luxembourg SA variants and bearer-share entries [Finding #11129].

The company was a closed Luxembourg société anonyme operating as the holding tier above SPQR's investment activity. SEC EDGAR DEF 14A filings for Equus Total Return Inc, together with UK Companies House and SEC disclosures, record that Alessandro Benedetti served as a director of SPQR Capital Holdings SA from August 2010 onward [Finding #847][SEC:878932]. The Luxembourg arm operated alongside SPQR Capital Services Sagl, a Lugano entity registered on 17 March 2011 under company number CHE-496.390.425 with capital of CHF 20,000 and chair Alessandro Benedetti [Finding #11215][Finding #11103]. The broader SPQR group also included UK and Cayman entities such as SPQR Capital (Cayman) Ltd, with SPQR Capital Holding SA sitting at the Luxembourg apex of the structure [Finding #11114][Finding #11221].

sections.title: Directors and the 1 March 2016 Simultaneous Installation
sections.content:
The Luxembourg RCS director timeline retrieved via NorthData shows three SPQR Capital Holding SA directors appointed on the same day, 1 March 2016: Alessandro Benedetti as chair, Bertrand G. des Pallières, and Mathieu Villaume [Finding #11215][REG:LU:B150334]. Villaume departed on 7 February 2018, and Michel Thill served briefly between October 2021 and August 2022 [Finding #11215]. The simultaneous appointment coincided with the active phase of the Wind Hellas / TIM Hellas creditor litigation against Naguib Sawiris's Weather Investments. Analysis of the registry record suggests the three-handed board — a private-equity principal, a hedge-fund founder, and a Luxembourg corporate-administration director — fits a common Luxembourg fund-vehicle governance shape rather than a unique structural design, a reading offered as interpretation rather than established fact [Finding #11226].

Each director's record is documented in independent registry sources. UK Companies House filings, ICIJ Paradise Papers data, and OCCRP Aleph entries for Benedetti record his concurrent roles as CEO of SAE Capital Ltd, executive chairman of Equus Total Return Inc (NYSE: EQS, June 2011 – June 2014), and designated member of Asherco LLP (UK OC379532) [Finding #11103][Finding #847][SEC:878932]. Des Pallières's career, recorded by UK Companies House and Luxembourg RCS filings, spans Managing Director and Global Head of Structured Credit at JPMorgan (1992–2005), Managing Director and Global Head of Principal Finance at Deutsche Bank (2005–2007), and CEO/founder of SPQR Capital Holdings SA from 2010 onward [Finding #11221][Finding #11101][Finding #11114]. Villaume's NorthData profile lists more than 21 active Luxembourg mandates including Compagnie Du Saleve SA and the Knightsbridge Capital Partners Holding I/II/III SA series [Finding #11223][Finding #11129].

On the registry filings, the full legal name of des Pallières is "Bertrand Ghislain Yves Gauquelin des Pallières," and an earlier reference to him as "Stéphane des Pallières" was a misidentification that finding #11215 explicitly corrects [Finding #11129][Finding #11215][Finding #11221]. Benedetti and "Bertrand Gauquelin" had jointly resigned from SPQR on 18 December 2015, with the 1 March 2016 reinstallation of all three directors following shortly after [Finding #11129].

sections.title: Wind Hellas / TIM Hellas Creditor Activity
sections.content:
SPQR Capital was a noteholder in the Wind Hellas / TIM Hellas Greek telecommunications creditor dispute that culminated in Naguib Sawiris's Weather Investments acquiring the group out of administration. The trade publication privatefundscfo.com reported SPQR among the bondholders that suffered effectively total losses on their subordinated position [Finding #11149]. SPQR was not a named plaintiff in Adversary Proceeding 14-01848 before Hon. Martin Glenn in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York, but participated as a beneficial holder represented through Wilmington Trust and the Cortlandt Street Recovery litigation-funding vehicle [Finding #11149].

Bertrand G. des Pallières publicly called on the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales to investigate Ernst & Young over the Wind Hellas administration, after SPQR Capital and other junior bondholders were reported to have lost millions when Sawiris's Weather Investments wiped approximately GBP 1.3 billion of debt acquiring the group out of administration [Finding #11221]. The Independent's article of 28 October 2015 by Jim Armitage and Mark Hollingsworth, titled "The private equity giants, the Greek target, and a Trojan horse," identifies "SPQR Capital's Bertrand des Pallieres" as the on-the-record creditor source for that piece [Finding #11125].

The related litigation has a detailed procedural history, including the Hon. Martin Glenn opinions Hosking I through Hosking IV (2015–2016), the forum non conveniens stay granted on 19 August 2016, the termination of the adversary proceeding on 4 August 2022, and the closure of the Chapter 15 case on 21 November 2022 [Finding #11149]. On 23 December 2015 the Luxembourg Tribunal d'Arrondissement held that the Convertible Preferred Equity Certificates at issue were debt instruments not subject to Luxembourg companies-law illegal-dividend rules — a ruling that, on the documentary record, foreclosed the parallel "fraudulent dividend" theory advanced in the United States and United Kingdom [Finding #11149].

sections.title: Sister Entity: SPQR Capital Services Sagl
sections.content:
SPQR Capital Services Sagl is the Swiss arm of the SPQR group, registered with the Lugano commercial register on 17 March 2011 under company number CHE-496.390.425 with subscribed capital of CHF 20,000 and chair Alessandro Benedetti [Finding #11215][Finding #11103]. The Lugano entity sits inside Benedetti's broader Swiss-Italian group of companies alongside Schwarzfield SA (Luxembourg/Geneva), Schwarzfield Services SAGL (Lugano), and a recorded set of approximately 22 entities across Italy, the United Kingdom, Luxembourg, Switzerland, the British Virgin Islands, Malta, the United States, France, the Netherlands, and Panama [Finding #11103].

Benedetti's UK Companies House and SEC EDGAR records situate SPQR Capital Services Sagl alongside SAE Capital Ltd (UK), Asherco LLP (UK OC379532), Tree of Life Limited (Malta C67345, ICIJ Paradise Papers), and Barkmere Group Ltd (BVI) — the BVI entity that the Wall Street Journal of 27 February 2020 reported received USD 500,000 from Rajeev Misra [Finding #11103]. That cross-referencing of registry and ICIJ data is presented here as analysis rather than as a single sourced fact.

sections.title: Liquidation and Wind-Down
sections.content:
The Luxembourg RCS record retrieved via NorthData shows SPQR Capital Holding SA entering liquidation on 16 March 2023 under court-appointed liquidator Christian Steinmetz [Finding #11215][REG:LU:B150334]. Mathieu Villaume had departed the board approximately five years earlier, on 7 February 2018, and the brief October 2021 – August 2022 directorship of Michel Thill ended several months before the liquidation filing [Finding #11215][Finding #11223].

By the time of the OneIM team-page disclosure, Bertrand G. des Pallières had moved into a Partner – Private Credit role at OneIM, the Abu Dhabi vehicle of Rajeev Misra [Finding #11114]. Cross-referencing the filings suggests this move carried the Centricus and SPQR-era circle into the OneIM vehicle within the broader Mubadala/Royal Group ecosystem associated with Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, an interpretation offered as analysis rather than as a documented fact [Finding #11114].

sections.title: Significance
sections.content:
SPQR Capital Holding SA is the Luxembourg vehicle that anchors the recurring Benedetti–des Pallières–Villaume director set across the wider group of companies reconstructed from corporate filings [Finding #11103][Finding #11221]. The same three-handed board configuration appears in Attali Investment Partners Ltd (UK 07138407), Equus Total Return Inc (NYSE: EQS), Cadogan Petroleum plc, Bitfury Group Limited (UK 11441275), and the Methorios Capital LLP corporate-director chain. On the documentary record, that recurring board is the connection between the SoftBank Vision Fund principal Rajeev Misra and the Italian financier Alessandro Benedetti [Finding #11101][Finding #11221].

Analysis of the registry data and ICIJ Paradise Papers node 56009779 suggests that Mathieu Villaume's simultaneous mandates at SPQR Capital Holding SA, Compagnie Du Saleve SA (the Five Arrows AutoBench Holding portfolio entity), and the Knightsbridge Capital Partners Holding I/II/III SA series link the Benedetti–des Pallières group to the Rothschild & Co private-equity arm on the same Luxembourg address [Finding #11166]. The Wall Street Journal coverage of 27 February 2020 is the only public reporting stream catalogued here that names des Pallières as the introducer between Misra and Benedetti [Finding #11101]. The company thus serves as the connecting record — the registered vehicle whose sequence of director appointments joins the Wind Hellas creditor litigation, the Bitfury Group governance ties, and the Five Arrows / Rothschild address overlap [Finding #11149][Finding #11211][Finding #11114].

open_questions: Which counterparties received SPQR Capital Holding SA's Wind Hellas creditor distribution recoveries through the Cortlandt Street Recovery / Wilmington Trust funding chain, and were any of those flows recorded in Luxembourg or US bankruptcy filings beyond the materials reviewed here?

What was the originating share-capital subscription and ultimate beneficial-owner structure of SPQR Capital Holding SA at the 2010 incorporation, and is there a Luxembourg RCS or ICIJ Open Corporates record for the original three-person founding team (des Pallières, Malik Chaabouni, Moez Ben-Zid)?

Did the 16 March 2023 liquidator Christian Steinmetz file a final liquidation report with the Luxembourg RCS that itemises remaining SPQR assets and any transfer of holdings to OneIM or successor vehicles in the Misra–Tahnoon ecosystem?

Which of the eleven Panama Papers entities at 12 rue Guillaume Schneider share officers, beneficial owners, or counterparties with SPQR Capital Holding SA beyond the documented overlap with Compagnie Du Saleve SA?

What is the relationship, if any, between SPQR Capital Holding SA and the Bitfury Group Limited (UK 11441275) governance — that is, does Bitfury appear in any SPQR portfolio filing, or is the link through des Pallières's personal directorship only?
